title: The tracker mirror's per-write path is the next structural cut
description:
internal/reconcile/tracker.go's publish path pays, for every tracker write: a temp index, read-tree, add -A, write-tree, diff-tree (stagedTree), then commit-tree plus a `reset --hard` that rewrites the whole working tree — about 6 processes plus the reset's file churn per write, 31 resets in one fixture e2e test, next to the ~15 commit-trees that remain there after the store's write path changed. The tracker's change sets already ride the store's fast-import (StageChanges); what remains expensive is the mirror's own diff-and-commit dance. A tick that computes the change set without the throwaway index (git diff --name-status against the base, then hash-object per changed file, or one fast-import for the local mirror commit) would cut the fixture pass by roughly a further 10-15% — it needs the same care this tick took: the change set must be exactly what add -A + diff-tree computes, because tracker records are durable evidence.
evidence: internal/reconcile/tracker.go:339 (stagedTree) and tracker.go:380-387 (stage's commit-tree + reset --hard); 31 reset --hard invocations per fixture pass in the wrapper profile
